text.String: Linux distributions combine the kernel with utilities, libraries, package managers, and applications.

Linux is an operating system kernel used by many different operating systems and distributions. Linux is widely used on servers, personal computers, embedded devices, and cloud infrastructure. The Linux kernel manages hardware resources and provides essential services to applications. Processes are running programs managed by the operating system. Linux uses virtual memory to give processes an isolated address space. The scheduler decides which processes receive CPU time. Filesystems organize data stored on disks and other storage devices. Linux supports many filesystems including ext4 and XFS. The command line is an important part of Linux administration.

Computer networking allows devices to communicate and exchange information. A network can connect computers within a local area or across the internet. IP addresses identify network interfaces and allow packets to be routed between networks. IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery of data between applications. TCP uses connections and retransmission to handle lost packets. UDP provides a simpler connectionless transport mechanism without guaranteeing delivery. DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. HTTP is an application protocol commonly used to transfer web resources. HTTPS adds encryption and authentication to HTTP using TLS.
Git is useful because it provides distributed history, branching, merging, and tools for collaborating on software projects.

Remote repositories allow developers to share changes with other machines and team members. The git clone command creates a local copy of a remote repository. The git fetch command downloads changes from a remote repository without changing the current branch. The git pull command retrieves remote changes and integrates them into the current branch. The git push command uploads local commits to a remote repository. Tags can identify important commits such as software releases. Git log displays commit history and can help developers inspect previous changes. Git diff shows differences between versions of files.

Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety and performance. Rust provides memory safety without requiring a garbage collector. The language is useful for building fast and reliable software.

Deadlocks can occur when processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other. Operating systems use scheduling algorithms to decide how CPU time is distributed. Common scheduling approaches include first-come-first-served, shortest-job-first, priority scheduling, and round-robin scheduling. Operating systems also provide security mechanisms for controlling access to files, processes, memory, and hardware resources.

A database is a system for storing and retrieving structured information. Relational databases organize information into tables containing rows and columns. Each row represents a record and each column represents an attribute. SQL is commonly used to query relational databases. A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table. Foreign keys establish relationships between tables. Database indexes improve query performance by providing efficient ways to locate records. An index can reduce the amount of data that a database needs to examine during a query. Transactions allow multiple database operations to be treated as a single unit of work.

The command line is an important part of Linux administration. Common commands include ls, cd, cp, mv, and grep. Permissions control which users can read, write, or execute files. Linux uses users and groups to manage access to system resources. The root user has extensive privileges over the system. Services can run in the background and provide functionality such as networking or web hosting. System logs help administrators diagnose problems. Linux networking provides tools for inspecting interfaces, routes, and connections. Shell scripts can automate repetitive administrative tasks. Package managers are used to install and update software.

Memory pages can be mapped to physical memory or stored on disk when necessary. A page fault occurs when a process accesses a page that is not currently available in physical memory. The operating system uses page tables to translate virtual addresses into physical addresses. File systems organize persistent data into files and directories. Device drivers allow the operating system to communicate with hardware devices. System calls provide an interface through which applications request services from the operating system. Applications can use system calls to open files, create processes, allocate memory, and communicate with devices.

Applications can use system calls to open files, create processes, allocate memory, and communicate with devices. User mode restricts applications from directly performing privileged operations. Kernel mode allows the operating system to perform privileged operations. Interrupts allow hardware devices to notify the processor that an event requires attention. The operating system also provides mechanisms for processes to communicate and synchronize. Threads allow multiple execution paths to exist within a process. Locks and other synchronization mechanisms help protect shared data from concurrent access. Deadlocks can occur when processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
The language is useful for building fast and reliable software.
Package managers are used to install and update software. Linux distributions combine the kernel with utilities, libraries, package managers, and applications.
Python has many machine learning libraries including PyTorch and scikit-learn.

Backups protect data against accidental deletion and hardware failures. Replication can maintain copies of data on multiple database servers. Database systems can be optimized through indexes, query design, caching, and appropriate hardware.

Transactions allow multiple database operations to be treated as a single unit of work. Transactions commonly provide atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. These properties are known as ACID. Atomicity means that a transaction succeeds completely or fails completely. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions interact with each other. Durability means committed changes survive failures. Database normalization reduces unnecessary duplication of information. Joins allow queries to combine related data from multiple tables. A database query optimizer chooses an efficient strategy for executing a query. Backups protect data against accidental deletion and hardware failures.

HTTPS adds encryption and authentication to HTTP using TLS. Routers forward packets between different networks. Switches connect devices within a local network. A port identifies a network service associated with a transport protocol. Firewalls control network traffic according to configured rules. Latency describes the time required for data to travel between endpoints. Bandwidth describes the capacity of a network connection. Packet loss occurs when packets fail to reach their destination. Network troubleshooting can involve checking interfaces, routes, DNS configuration, connectivity, and service availability. Tools such as ping, traceroute, curl, and netstat can help diagnose networking problems.
Operating systems also provide security mechanisms for controlling access to files, processes, memory, and hardware resources.

An operating system manages computer hardware and provides services that allow application programs to run. The operating system manages processes, memory, storage, devices, and security. A process is a program that is currently executing. The operating system scheduler determines which process receives CPU time. Processes can move between states such as ready, running, and waiting. Context switching allows the CPU to move from one process to another. Virtual memory gives processes the appearance of having a large private memory space. Memory pages can be mapped to physical memory or stored on disk when necessary.

A branch is a movable reference to a series of commits. Branches allow developers to work on different features without immediately changing the main development line. The git switch command can be used to move between branches. Merging combines changes from different branches. A merge conflict can occur when Git cannot automatically combine changes. Developers must manually resolve conflicting changes before completing the merge. Git rebase can replay commits onto a different base commit and can produce a cleaner project history. Remote repositories allow developers to share changes with other machines and team members.
Tools such as ping, traceroute, curl, and netstat can help diagnose networking problems.

Git diff shows differences between versions of files. Git status reports the current state of the working tree and staging area. Git reset can move references or modify the staging area depending on how it is used. Git stash temporarily saves uncommitted changes so that developers can switch tasks. Git is useful because it provides distributed history, branching, merging, and tools for collaborating on software projects.
Database systems can be optimized through indexes, query design, caching, and appropriate hardware.

Python is widely used for machine learning and data science. Machine learning models learn patterns from data and can make predictions on new examples. Embeddings represent text, images, or other information as numerical vectors. Vector similarity can be used to find items that are semantically related. Neural networks are commonly used to learn useful representations from large datasets. Python has many machine learning libraries including PyTorch and scikit-learn.

Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety and performance. Rust provides memory safety without requiring a garbage collector. Ownership is one of the core concepts in Rust and controls how memory is managed. Borrowing allows Rust programs to reference data without taking ownership. The Rust compiler checks ownership and borrowing rules at compile time. Rust is commonly used for systems programming, web services, command line tools, and embedded software. Concurrency is another important feature of Rust because the type system helps prevent many data races. Cargo is the package manager and build system used by Rust projects.

Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in files and coordinate work between developers. A Git repository stores the history of a project and contains information about commits, branches, and other objects. A commit records a snapshot of changes along with metadata such as the author and message. The staging area allows developers to select which changes should be included in the next commit. The git add command places changes into the staging area. The git commit command creates a new commit from staged changes. A branch is a movable reference to a series of commits.
Cargo is the package manager and build system used by Rust projects.
